title: Global Mean Sea Level 1993-2025
description: This animation shows the rise in global mean sea level from 1993 to 2023 based on data from a series of five international satellites.
full_text: This animation shows the rise in global mean sea level from 1993 to 2023 based on data from a series of five international satellites. This animation shows the rise in global mean sea level from 1993 to 2023 based on data from a series of five international satellites. This NASA-led analysis is based on a sea level data set featuring more than 30 years of satellite observations, starting with the U.S.-French TOPEX/Poseidon mission, which launched in 1992. The [Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich mission](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/sentinel-6-michael-freilich/), which launched in November 2020, is the latest in the series of satellites that have contributed to this sea level record. [Sentinal-6B](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/sentinel-6b/) which launched in 2025 will help continue these observations into the future. The data use to create these graphs is available [here.](https://zenodo.org/records/7702315) Learn more about sea level rise [here.](https://earth.gov/sealevel) This animation shows the rise in global mean sea level from 1993 to 2024 based on data from a series of five international satellites.
